newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya, Russia may sign peace deal next week.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya, Russia may sign peace deal next week.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov may sign an accord on political settlement next week in Moscow, Interfax news agency said on Friday, quoting Maskhadov's spokesman.

The spokesman, Kazbek Khadzhiyev, said one point in the accord, aimed at turning a ceasefire between Russia and Chechnya into lasting peace, has not been agreed yet and the two presidents were expected to iron out the differences during face-to-face talks due to take place between next Monday and May 10.

Russian officials were not immediately availiable for comment. Russia and Chechnya agreed a ceasefire last summer after 21 months of war in which tens of thousands were killed, but talks have stalled on a political and economic settlement.

Maskhadov has been insisting on full independence. Moscow will not grant that and is offering what it calls broad sovereignity inside Russia. It is holding back funds to rebuild the Chechen economy until a final peace accord is signed.

The situation around Chechnya deteriorated badly over the past week after a spate of violence in the regions neighbouring Chechnya, including fatal bomb attacks and the murder of an official in which some Russian officials saw "a Chechen link".

It appeared that the agreement about Makskhadov's visit to Moscow came during talks between Russian security officials and Chechen bosses held hastily in the Chechen capital Grozny on Wednesday and aimed at easing tension in the North Caucasus.
